subject: SIGN clause
notes: WITNESSED (kb/Work PB803, owner decision 2026-09-09 questions 28+29). GR4's obligation has TWO halves and both are now pinned by a golden rather than only by a probe. POSITION: a signed item with no SIGN clause takes the TRAILING fused sign -- `12L` for -123 -- and conformance:cases/13.18.52-SIGN/pb803_sign_default_representation makes that claim REFUTABLE by comparing it against an item that writes SIGN IS TRAILING (must be equal) and one that writes SIGN IS LEADING (must differ, `J23`). REPRESENTATION: the characters are now the compile option --sign-encoding, whose default `ibm` is the previous fixed table (positive {ABCDEFGHI / negative }JKLMNOPQR) and whose `ascii` value is GnuCOBOL's -fsign=ascii (positive digits untouched / negative p-y); conformance:wiseowl/cases/13.18.52-SIGN/pb803_sign_encoding_ascii compiles under `*> options: sign-encoding=ascii` and pins `123t` / `q234`, so the LATITUDE ITSELF is exercised and not merely one choice within it. WIDTH: a one-byte sentinel immediately after the signed item inside the same group answers `12L|` only for a 3-character item, so GR5 a)'s no-extra-position consequence cannot drift unobserved. EDITION INDEPENDENCE is now a claim with a witness rather than an assumption: conformance:cases/13.18.52-SIGN/pb803_sign_default_representation_85 repeats the representation, the position and the valid-set legs at COBOL-85 (no intrinsic, so the width rides entirely on the sentinel).
